record.context_brief: Integer solutions for two cubic-sum equations
record.original_question: Find a complete and mathematically usable description of all integer solutions to the Diophantine equations y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1 and y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1.

evidence.quote: Given a polynomial Diophantine equation (1), one may ask whether its set of integer solutions can be described in any "reasonable" way.
Nevertheless, the smallest equations for which we currently do not know a "satisfiable" answer are the equations y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1 (3) and y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1. (4)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Provide a complete and mathematically usable description of the set of all integer triples (x, y, z) ∈ ℤ³ satisfying each of the following Diophantine equations:

(a) y² + z² = x³ + 1,
(b) y² + z² = x³ − 1.

By a "complete and mathematically usable description" we mean either an explicit finite list of parametric families (each given by polynomial or otherwise algorithmically describable formulas in finitely many integer parameters) whose union is exactly the solution set, or an effective procedure that, given any bound N, outputs all integer solutions with max(|x|,|y|,|z|) ≤ N together with a proof that no others exist. Determine whether such a description exists for each of (a) and (b), and exhibit it.
artifact.status_search_result: A standard web search did not surface a published complete description of the integer solution sets of y² + z² = x³ ± 1. These equations are noted as among the smallest cubic Diophantine equations for which no satisfactory description of all integer solutions is currently known, and no resolution has been located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Diophantine equation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General overview of Diophantine equations; no description of integer solutions to y^2+z^2=x^3±1 is given.
status_evidence.claim: No general method or complete solution set for these particular cubic equations is reported in standard references.
